models.collectorNote: Early Quadrifoglios are the value in fast sedans, budget for the Alfa tax: specialist maintenance and electrical patience. 2021-on cars are the sorted ones.

generations.name: Giulia / Quadrifoglio
generations.note: Carbon propshaft, 50:50 balance, and steering quicker than a 3 Series'. The Quadrifoglio launched at 505 hp; the GTA and GTAm specials are the collector-grade cars.

models.intro: Project Giorgio: Alfa poached Ferrari engineers, spent billions, and produced a rear-drive sedan whose Quadrifoglio variant, with a Ferrari-derived twin-turbo V6, reset the sports-sedan benchmark.
models.name: Giulia
models.photoCredit: Photo: Alexander Migl, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

photos.caption: Alfa Romeo Giulia Veloce (952), front 3/4
photos.credit: Photo: Alexander Migl, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

generations.name: Stelvio / Quadrifoglio
generations.note: Same Giorgio bones as the Giulia, standard all-wheel drive, and the Quadrifoglio's 2.9 V6 made it the fastest SUV around the 'Ring at 7:51.7 in 2017.

models.intro: The Giulia's platform under an SUV body, named for the pass with 48 hairpins. The Quadrifoglio version held the Nürburgring SUV lap record on launch.
models.name: Stelvio
models.photoCredit: Photo: KGC626, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

photos.caption: 2017 Alfa-Romeo Stelvio Kragujevac
photos.credit: Photo: KGC626, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

models.collectorNote: Duettos lead the market; Series 4 cars are the drive-it bargain. Rust in the sills and floors is the whole negotiation, the twin-cam is the easy part.

generations.name: Duetto
generations.note: The 'osso di seppia' cuttlefish-bone tail. A 1.6 twin-cam with an alloy head and twin Webers when British rivals ran pushrods.

generations.name: Spider Veloce
generations.note: The final, cleaned-up Spider: body-colour bumpers, power steering, Bosch injection. The most usable of the breed and still the prettiest cheap Italian roadster.

models.intro: The Duetto: Pininfarina's round-tail roadster, Dustin Hoffman's co-star in The Graduate, and one of the longest-lived sports car designs ever, 28 years with the same basic body.
models.name: Spider
models.photoCredit: Photo: Ermell, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

photos.caption: Spider 2000 Veloce (Series 2), on road
photos.credit: Photo: Ermell, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

models.collectorNote: Values have been firm since new. The Spider is rarer in practice, fewer were ordered, and the coupé is the design icon. Both are museum-grade already.

generations.name: 8C Competizione / Spider
generations.note: The name revives the 8C racers of the 1930s. Transaxle gearbox, carbon everywhere, and a crossplane V8 soundtrack no modern turbo Alfa matches.

models.intro: A concept car Alfa actually built: carbon body over a Maserati-derived chassis with Ferrari's 4.7 V8 up front. 500 coupés, then 500 Spiders, all sold before production began.
models.name: 8C Competizione
models.photoCredit: Photo: Calreyn88, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

photos.caption: 2009 Alfa Romeo 8C Competizione
photos.credit: Photo: Calreyn88, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

models.collectorNote: Genuine GTAs are seven-figure-adjacent in Europe and thick with replicas, verify chassis numbers against the register before anything else. A good 2000 GTV is the driver's sweet spot.

generations.name: Sprint GT / GTV
generations.note: The 'step front' came from the gap between bonnet and grille panel. All-alloy twin-cam engines from 1.3 to 2.0 litres, five-speed boxes, discs all round, a specification British rivals took a decade to match.

generations.name: GTA 1600
generations.note: The 'A' stands for alleggerita, lightened. Aluminium panels, magnesium wheels, 115 hp from 1.6 litres, and back-to-back European Touring Car titles.

models.intro: Bertone's stepped-nose coupé, styled by a young Giorgetto Giugiaro. The GTA variant, aluminium skin, twin-plug head, owned European touring car racing in the late 1960s.
models.name: Giulia Sprint GT

models.collectorNote: The 1939 Lungo Spider made $19,800,000 at RM Sotheby's Monterey in 2016, then the most expensive pre-war car ever sold at auction. A 1939 Touring Berlinetta made €16,745,000 at Artcurial in Paris in 2019.

generations.name: 8C 2900B Corto
generations.note: The short-chassis cars carried spider and berlinetta bodies, with independent suspension all round and a rear transaxle, technology no rival matched. Road tune gave 180 hp from the 2.9 litre twin-cam eight.

generations.name: 8C 2900B Lungo
generations.note: The long-chassis Lungo was the grand tourer of the pair, and Touring's berlinettas and spiders on it are among the most admired pre-war bodies ever made. The 2900 family owned the Mille Miglia, winning in 1936, 1937, 1938 and again in 1947.

models.intro: Vittorio Jano's masterpiece took the Grand Prix Tipo B's twin-supercharged straight-eight and dressed it in Touring's Superleggera aluminium. Around 30 chassis were built in short Corto and long Lungo forms. Nothing else of the 1930s combined this speed, this engineering and this beauty in one car.
